key_insight: Interleaving discrete semantic, acoustic, and text tokens in a single next-token prediction model enables scalable native audio foundation models that jointly capture content, timbre, and language for both high-fidelity audio generation and cross-modal tasks.
problem_solved: Overcomes limitations of text-first or semantic-only audio approaches by providing a unified, native-audio modeling approach that preserves acoustic detail while supporting semantic/text alignment and generation at scale.
method: Discretize audio into separate token streams for semantic content and acoustic/details, plus text tokens, then interleave them into a single sequence for autoregressive next-token prediction.
Scale transformer training on large paired audio–text and unlabeled audio corpora to learn joint representations that support generation, transcription, and cross-modal tasks.
Evaluate empirically across fidelity, semantic accuracy, and downstream tasks to demonstrate trade-offs and scaling behavior between acoustic detail and semantic modeling.
impact: Provides practitioners a unified modeling recipe to build open, scalable audio foundation models that improve generation fidelity and multimodal capabilities, enabling more capable speech, music, and general audio systems.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing three token streams (semantic, acoustic, text) being interleaved into one transformer input and producing mixed outputs.
Timeline view illustrating token interleaving over a short audio clip (labels for semantic vs acoustic vs text tokens).
Scaling/ablation plots: model size or data scale vs metrics for acoustic fidelity and semantic accuracy to show trade-offs.
Examples panel with input prompt/text → generated waveform/spectrogram + transcription and semantic labels.
paper_title: Scaling Open Discrete Audio Foundation Models with Interleaved Semantic, Acoustic, and Text Tokens
paper_authors: Potsawee Manakul, Woody Haosheng Gan, Martijn Bartelds, Guangzhi Sun, William Held
